course_description: Exploring Materials: scientific inquiry, design and evidence.
title: Science in action: evidence, design and everyday decisions
overview: A learner-centred investigation of how scientists use evidence, repeatable methods, creativity and community review.
learning_outcomes: Explain key characteristics of science with everyday examples.
Use evidence to improve a small design project.
Communicate a conclusion and its evidence clearly.
prior_knowledge: Learners recall a question they have investigated at home, in school or in the community.
engage: Show two claims about a local issue, such as which fertiliser helps seedlings grow best. Learners vote, then identify what evidence would change their minds.
investigate: In mixed-role teams, plan a fair mini-investigation or analyse a supplied set of plant-growth observations. Teams identify the question, variables, evidence and limits.
explain: Use a claim-evidence-reasoning discussion to connect observations to empirical evidence, repeatability, objectivity and creative problem-solving.
elaborate: Teams create a one-page science-in-action poster for cooking, farming, health or school life and receive peer feedback using an evidence checklist.
practical_work: Design challenge: compare two conditions in a simple seedling or solar-oven investigation, record observations in a table and improve the design after feedback.
safety_notes: Follow teacher guidance for heat, cutting tools, fertilisers and outdoor work. Do not taste experimental materials.
assessment: Exit ticket: explain one characteristic of science, cite one item of evidence and state one change that would make an investigation fairer.
extension: Extension / enrichment: investigate how a Ghanaian science-related innovation uses evidence and iteration.

course_title: SHS 1 Section 2 - Solids and Binary Compounds
course_description: Exploring Materials: properties, classification and uses of solids.
title: Materials detectives: solids, properties and binary compounds
overview: Learners classify common solids from observable evidence and connect composition to useful properties.
learning_outcomes: Classify materials as metals, semi-metals or non-metals using evidence.
Relate lustre, conductivity and hardness to everyday uses.
Distinguish binary ionic and binary covalent compounds.
prior_knowledge: Learners bring examples of materials used in a phone, bicycle, cooking pot or classroom desk.
engage: Present a mystery-material tray. Teams predict what each item is used for and justify their prediction from observable properties.
investigate: At stations, learners test or observe lustre, scratch resistance and low-voltage conductivity, then use a classification grid to compare evidence.
explain: Facilitate a gallery walk where groups explain how material properties make objects suitable for particular jobs; introduce binary-compound naming through examples.
elaborate: Learners recommend a material for a local design brief, such as a cooking utensil or simple electrical contact, and defend the choice with evidence.
practical_work: Property-testing circuit: record observations for selected solids, classify them and write an evidence-based recommendation.
safety_notes: Use only teacher-approved low-voltage circuits. Handle sharp edges, samples and sandpaper carefully; never connect materials to mains electricity.
assessment: Individual evidence card: classify an unfamiliar sample, state two observed properties and explain one likely use.
extension: Extension / enrichment: research corrosion prevention for a locally used metal object.

course_description: Processes for Living: movement of substances in living and non-living media.
title: Particles on the move: diffusion and osmosis
overview: An evidence-led study of particle movement in gases, solutions and living tissues.
alignment_status: Learning-module source; official code awaiting verified curriculum import
learning_outcomes: Explain diffusion as movement from higher to lower concentration.
Use osmosis to account for changes in model cells and plant tissues.
Interpret observations using a concentration gradient.
prior_knowledge: Learners recall dissolving a drink mix or noticing a smell spread through a room.
engage: Place a scent source at one side of the room or show a short time-lapse. Learners predict which observer notices it first and why.
investigate: Groups observe diffusion in a safe teacher-prepared demonstration and compare model-cell or potato-tissue results from different solutions.
explain: Learners draw particle diagrams before and after an investigation and use arrows to explain movement without treating particles as purposeful agents.
elaborate: Pairs solve a home-and-community scenario involving food preservation, plant watering or gas exchange, then create a short explanation for another pair.
practical_work: Record initial and final measurements for model cells or potato tissues, construct a results table and explain the pattern using water movement.
safety_notes: Use teacher-prepared solutions and potassium permanganate with care. Do not consume laboratory solutions; wash hands after handling plant tissue.
assessment: Four-corner diagnostic: learners select and justify the correct explanation for a diffusion or osmosis scenario, then revise after peer challenge.
extension: Extension / enrichment: compare osmosis in a food-preservation context with osmosis in plant cells.

course_title: SHS 1 Section 4 - Reproduction in Plants and Humans
course_description: Processes for Living: reproduction, life cycles and responsible health learning.
title: Life continues: reproduction, life cycles and responsible choices
overview: A respectful, age-appropriate exploration of plant and human reproduction through models, life-cycle evidence and guided discussion.
source_section: Year 1 Section 4: Reproduction in Plants and Humans
alignment_status: Learning-module source; official code awaiting verified curriculum import
learning_outcomes: Describe sexual and asexual reproduction in plants.
Explain how pollination and seed dispersal support plant life cycles.
Use accurate, respectful language when discussing human reproductive health.
prior_knowledge: Learners identify how a familiar plant makes new plants and agree discussion norms for sensitive health content.
engage: Use a flower or model as a mystery object: learners predict how pollen could reach the stigma and compare insect and wind routes.
investigate: Teams model pollination, compare propagation techniques and sequence a flowering-plant life cycle using labelled evidence cards.
explain: Teacher-guided modelling clarifies structures, processes and vocabulary; learners ask anonymous questions through a question box where appropriate.
elaborate: Groups advise a school garden on whether to use seed, cutting, grafting or layering for a chosen plant and justify the recommendation.
practical_work: Carry out a pollination simulation or supervised vegetative-propagation observation, recording prediction, method, evidence and limitations.
safety_notes: Use tools only with supervision. Keep discussions factual, respectful and age-appropriate; protect privacy and avoid personal disclosures.
assessment: Learners annotate a life-cycle diagram and submit a claim-evidence explanation comparing sexual and asexual reproduction.
extension: Extension / enrichment: investigate an appropriate local crop-propagation practice with a grower or extension officer.

course_description: Vigour Behind Life: renewable energy and design thinking.
title: Power from sunlight: solar panels for Ghanaian communities
overview: Learners investigate photovoltaic energy, measure output under changing conditions and propose a locally relevant solar solution.
alignment_status: Learning-module source; official code awaiting verified curriculum import
learning_outcomes: Describe how solar panels convert light into electrical energy.
Interpret voltage, current and power measurements.
Design a realistic solar-energy solution using local constraints.
prior_knowledge: Learners list ways sunlight supports life and identify an energy-use challenge at home or school.
engage: Compare photographs of a solar lantern, a rooftop system and a diesel generator. Learners rank which could help a selected community need and explain why.
investigate: Teams measure or analyse supplied voltage and current readings for a small solar panel under direct light, partial shade and artificial light.

safety_notes: Use only teacher-approved kits and multimeters. Avoid short circuits; do not stare at concentrated sunlight or handle hot equipment carelessly.
assessment: Design pitch: present an evidence-backed solar solution and answer a peer question about one trade-off.
extension: Extension / enrichment: compare a solar option with grid and fossil-fuel use using a local energy context.

course_description: Vigour Behind Life: forces, motion and interactions.
title: Forces everywhere: friction, gravity and motion
overview: A practical exploration of how forces change motion and how evidence helps learners reason about everyday design.
alignment_status: Learning-module source; official code awaiting verified curriculum import
learning_outcomes: Explain frictional, gravitational and other forces in familiar situations.
Use distance and time evidence to reason about velocity.
Evaluate useful and unwanted effects of friction.
prior_knowledge: Learners compare sliding on smooth and rough surfaces and identify forces they have felt while travelling or playing sport.
engage: Ask learners to predict which surface lets a block travel farthest, then make a visible prediction line before testing.
investigate: Groups test a consistent push across surfaces, measure distance or time, and compare force diagrams for the trials.
explain: Use group data to distinguish speed and velocity and to explain why friction can help or resist movement.

safety_notes: Keep tracks clear, secure stands, use light objects for dropping activities and follow teacher direction for ramps or spring scales.
assessment: Claim-evidence-reasoning paragraph: decide whether more friction is desirable in one real-life situation and support the decision.
extension: Extension / enrichment: investigate a local transport or sports design where controlling friction matters.

course_description: Vigour Behind Life: consumer electronics and simple circuits.
title: Inside everyday devices: components, circuits and amplification
overview: Learners identify electronic components, reason about circuit behaviour and build or simulate simple electronic systems.
alignment_status: Learning-module source; official code awaiting verified curriculum import
learning_outcomes: Identify common components in household electronic devices.
Explain the purpose of selected components in a circuit.
Build, test and improve a simple low-voltage circuit.
prior_knowledge: Learners list devices seen at a repair shop or at home and sketch what they think is inside one device.
engage: Use a labelled component mystery bag or images from a safe dismantled device. Learners match each component to a possible function.
investigate: Pairs construct or simulate an LED circuit, change polarity or a component, and record what changed and why.
explain: Build a shared component-function map and trace a simple signal path through an amplifier model.

assessment: Component challenge: identify a component, state its role and predict what changes if it is reversed, removed or adjusted.
extension: Extension / enrichment: research responsible electronic-waste handling and repair practices in the local community.

course_title: SHS 1 Section 8 - Promoting Health and Safety
course_description: Relationships with the Environment: hazards, lifestyle and health choices.
title: Health detectives: hazards, lifestyle and safe choices
overview: A community-connected inquiry into hazards, lifestyle disease prevention and evidence-informed health choices.
source_section: Year 1 Section 8: Promoting Health and Safety
alignment_status: Learning-module source; official code awaiting verified curriculum import
learning_outcomes: Identify biological, chemical and physical hazards.
Assess a local setting and propose proportionate risk controls.
Describe lifestyle-disease prevention using reliable health information.
prior_knowledge: Learners name one safety rule that protects people at home, in school or in a laboratory.
engage: Display a safe classroom or laboratory scene with hidden hazards. Learners work in pairs to spot, classify and prioritise them.
investigate: Groups complete a supervised hazard audit of an agreed school area, recording hazard, likely effect, type and practical control.
explain: Discuss the difference between hazard and risk, then compare how everyday choices can raise or reduce long-term health risks.
elaborate: Teams create a concise, evidence-based safety or health communication for a school audience, checking that it avoids stigma.
practical_work: Conduct a teacher-approved environmental hazard survey and submit a risk-control report with a labelled map or table.
safety_notes: Do not enter restricted areas, touch hazards or collect personal health information. Fieldwork must be supervised and respectful.
assessment: Risk-ranking task: justify which control should happen first and explain why it reduces harm.
extension: Extension / enrichment: compare a school health campaign with information from a trusted Ghanaian public-health source.

course_title: SHS 1 Section 9 - Production in Local Industry
course_description: Relationships with the Environment: scientific processes in local production.
title: Science in local industry: soap, food and process improvement
overview: Learners use observations from local production to connect chemistry, biology, safety and entrepreneurship.
source_section: Year 1 Section 9: Production in Local Industry
alignment_status: Learning-module source; official code awaiting verified curriculum import
learning_outcomes: Describe scientific stages in local soap and food production.
Relate saponification, fermentation and heat effects to observed production processes.
Evaluate safety, quality and environmental considerations in a local industry.
prior_knowledge: Learners share a familiar locally produced soap or food and identify steps they have observed.
engage: Sequence mixed-up picture cards showing a familiar production process. Learners explain what could go wrong if one stage is omitted.
investigate: Groups analyse a process flow for black soap or gari, annotate the science at each stage and compare two raw-material or process choices.
explain: Use the group flow maps to clarify physical and chemical changes, including saponification, fermentation and heating.
elaborate: Teams propose one safe, sustainable process improvement for a producer, considering materials, waste and product quality.
practical_work: Use a teacher-approved simulation or observation study to build a process diagram, record evidence and write a quality-and-safety evaluation.
safety_notes: Do not make soap or handle strong alkalis, hot oil or food-production machinery without trained adult supervision and approved controls.
assessment: Process explanation: annotate three stages with the science involved and justify one safety or quality-control decision.
extension: Extension / enrichment: interview or research a local producer with consent and compare evidence with the module process.

course_title: SHS 2 Section 1 - Nature of Different Liquids in Life
course_description: Year 2 learner module: acids, bases, solutions and pH.
title: Acids, bases and pH: investigate, test and explain
overview: A guided laboratory sequence on acid-base properties, neutralisation, solutions and pH measurement.
source_section: Year 2 Section 1: Nature of Different Liquids in Life
alignment_status: Learning-module source; official code awaiting verified curriculum import
learning_outcomes: Differentiate acids, bases and water using observable evidence.
Explain neutralisation and the uses of salts.
Measure and interpret pH safely.

investigate: In supervised stations, use indicators or supplied pH data to classify samples and record evidence in a pH table.

alignment_status: Learning-module source; official code awaiting verified curriculum import

Relate waste products to the organs that remove them.
Use models to explain filtration and regulation.
